provider: xAI Files API (Grok) + public CDN URLs

free_tier.stated: No published total-storage quota. Per-file 512 MB (some pages say 50 MB for the upload reference and 50 MiB for public URLs). Files are PERMANENT by default. `expires_after` is opt-in.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: Maximum file size: 512 MB per file.

retention.stated: Files default to permanent storage until you delete them.
retention.notes: Files default to permanent storage until you delete them.

egress.terms: Public URLs turn a stored file into a permanent, shareable link on the SpaceXSI CDN that anyone can open — no API key required.

interface_detail: OpenAI-compatible REST at https://api.x.ai/v1/files. POST upload, GET list, GET {id}, GET {id}/content (streams raw bytes, Content-Type application/octet-stream), DELETE, plus POST {id}/public-url and /public-url/revoke.
tooling: openai-python with base_url swapped to https://api.x.ai/v1; xai_sdk; curl
chaining: A file can have at most one active public URL at a time; calling create_public_url on a file that already has one returns the existing URL without producing a new one.
limits_note: Per-object-cap 512 MB (50 MB if you want a public URL. Public URLs are limited to images/video mime types). 'A file can have at most one active public URL at a time.' Public-URL creation can fail if the team hits its active-URL quota.
reliability_note: The absence of a published total quota is the finding, not an oversight. A third-party comparison site says outright 'no storage limit is stated. xAI says only that limits may vary slightly by platform or subscription'. Treat unverified. Files persist 'until you delete them'. Collections is a separate product with a 100 MB/file cap and requires credits in the account. Public URLs only cover image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp, video/mp4, video/webm. So the CDN path is media-only; arbitrary blobs must go through the authenticated content endpoint.

extras.unit_note: free_tier.unit is 'mixed' because the headline is denominated in MiB or KiB, which the schema enum does not carry; the verbatim free_tier.stated keeps the true unit. See the storage-dossier handover.
extras.verified_at_basis: the files page states a maximum file size of 512 MB per file
extras.quota_verbatim: No published total-storage quota. Per-file 512 MB (some pages say 50 MB for the upload reference and 50 MiB for public URLs). Files are PERMANENT by default — `expires_after` is opt-in.
extras.limits_verbatim: per-object-cap 512 MB (50 MB if you want a public URL — public URLs are limited to images/video mime types). 'A file can have at most one active public URL at a time.' Public-URL creation can fail if the team hits its active-URL quota.
extras.egress_verbatim: Every file can mint a public URL on files-cdn.x.ai, Cloudflare-fronted, no API key needed to fetch, no egress charge documented. URL is permanent if the file has no expiry and no expires_after is passed.
extras.chaining_verbatim: Upload -> create public URL -> Cloudflare caches it -> the CDN becomes the egress plane (same shape as the brief's §2.1 architecture, but the origin is the model provider). One active public URL per file at a time, but it is idempotent — re-calling returns the existing URL.
extras.tooling_verbatim: openai-python with base_url swapped to https://api.x.ai/v1; xai_sdk; curl
extras.interface_verbatim: OpenAI-compatible REST at https://api.x.ai/v1/files — POST upload, GET list, GET {id}, GET {id}/content (streams raw bytes, Content-Type application/octet-stream), DELETE, plus POST {id}/public-url and /public-url/revoke
extras.agent_focus: AI/agent platforms where file storage is a side effect of inference: /v1/files endpoints on LLM providers, chat-product file libraries (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini Notebook, Perplexity, Grok, Poe), RAG/index stores, and agent-infrastructure storage. Key question for each: is the storage number large, and can you get the bytes BACK?

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
